Linear contrasts of group-level coefficients

Source: R/coef-contrast.R
coef_contrast.Rd

Computes per-feature linear contrasts of the coefficients estimated by a regression-type reducer (for example "ols:voxelwise", "meta:fe_reg", "meta:re_reg", or the lmm:* reducers) on a realised GDS. The estimates are read from the coef:<term> assays and their sampling covariance from the cov:<a>:<b> assays (or, failing that, from the packed attachment returned by coef_cov_tri()); single-term contrasts need only se_coef:<term>.

Usage

coef_contrast(
  x,
  C,
  stat = c("auto", "t", "z"),
  df = NULL,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  joint = FALSE,
  name = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A realised gds produced by a regression-type reducer.

C

Contrast weights. A numeric vector named by term (one contrast), or a numeric matrix with one row per contrast and column names giving terms. Terms not named in C receive weight zero; names that are not coefficient terms of x are an error. Row names (or name) label the output assays.

stat

Reference distribution: "auto" (default) uses "t" when the reducer reported t_coef:<term> assays and "z" otherwise (e.g. the normal-approximation meta-regression reducers).

df

Optional degrees of freedom for stat = "t": a scalar or an array conformable with the coefficient assays. By default the per-term df_coef:<term> assays are used when present (taking the smallest over the terms a contrast involves, which is conservative), else df_res, else df.

alternative

Alternative hypothesis for single contrasts: "two.sided" (default), "greater", or "less". Joint tests are always upper-tailed.

joint

Logical; if TRUE, test all rows of a matrix C jointly with one F (or chi-square) statistic instead of one t (or z) test per row.

name

Optional label(s) for the output assays: one per row of C, or a single label when joint = TRUE (default "joint").

Value

x with additional assays, one family per contrast <name>:

  • single contrasts: contrast:<name> (estimate), se_contrast:<name>, t_contrast:<name> and df_contrast:<name> (or z_contrast:<name>), and p_contrast:<name>;

  • joint tests: F_contrast:<name> with df1_contrast:<name> and df2_contrast:<name> (or chi2_contrast:<name> with df1_contrast:<name>), and p_contrast:<name>.

Features whose contrast variance is not positive and finite are NA. Adjust the p-values with, e.g., posthoc(y, "fdr:bh", options = list(source = "p_contrast:<name>")).

Details

For each contrast \(c\) and feature the estimate is \(c^T \hat\beta\) with standard error \(\sqrt{c^T V c}\). With joint = TRUE the rows of C are tested together: \(F = (C\hat\beta)^T (C V C^T)^{-1} (C\hat\beta) / q\) on \((q, \nu)\) degrees of freedom for stat = "t", or the Wald statistic \(q F\) referred to \(\chi^2_q\) for stat = "z".

See also

coef_cov_tri(), coef_array(), reducer-ols-voxelwise

Examples

set.seed(1)
subj <- paste0("s", 1:12)
beta <- array(rnorm(4 * 12), c(4, 12, 1),
              dimnames = list(paste0("v", 1:4), subj, "c1"))
g <- as_gds(list(beta = beta, var = array(1, dim(beta), dimnames(beta))))
g <- with_col_data(g, data.frame(age = rnorm(12), dose = rnorm(12),
                                 row.names = subj))
fit <- compute(reduce(g, method = "ols:voxelwise", formula = ~ age + dose,
                      options = list(return_cov = "tri")))
res <- coef_contrast(fit, c(age = 1, dose = -1), name = "age_vs_dose")
assay(res, "t_contrast:age_vs_dose")[, 1, 1]
#> [1]  0.7589362  0.1038385  0.3222969 -0.8281914
